thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated container restart rate in pool 'prefill-gpu-pool-3' (OOM/sigkill) — 18 restarts in last 5m. Paging on-call.

anne_oncall: I'm on it, pulling logs now. Does this correlate with any deploys?

bob_infra: No deploys in the last hour. Seeing repeated CUDA timeouts + OOM during prefill on a subset of nodes. Sample from pod: 
```
[2023-10-19T02:33:12Z] runtime: cudaErrorKernelTimeout: driver timeout after 7000ms
[2023-10-19T02:33:12Z] mem: attempted alloc 14.3GB, available 12.1GB -> OOM -> container restart
```

anne_oncall: tagging @carla_sre for node-level checks. Which customer traffic is hitting this pool?

bob_infra: Traffic is predominantly long-context prefill requests (seq len 120k tokens window) from a single customer shard (cust-57). We pushed new prefetch behavior last month; looks like prefetch + huge context triggers sustained KV allocations and then kernel timeouts.

carla_sre: Oncall taking node diagnostics. Node 3 shows repeated GPU driver resets (nvidia-smi reports GPU 0 fault, process stuck in C state). I'm seeing kernel-level backtraces. Suspecting fragmentation + long-lived KV cache during prefill leads to large device allocations.

david_support: Customer-facing note: Customer 57 reports intermittent 502s and streaming cuts for long prompts since ~02:20Z. They're seeing ~10% request failures. I PMed customer with acknowledgement and we told them we're investigating.

anne_oncall: Live mitigation proposals: 1) Disable prefetch for prefills on this pool (fast). 2) Route cust-57 traffic to coldmodel/batched fallback (safer). 3) Enforce soft truncation on prefill sequences > 65k tokens. Which can we do quickly?

bob_infra: I can flip the prefetch flag on the pool now: endpoint: /pools/prefill-gpu-pool-3/config -> set prefetch=false. Doing it in 30s.

carla_sre: Prep commands I ran: 
```bash
# drain only prefill handler on node-3
kubectl cordon node-3 && kubectl drain node-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector=role=prefill
# check pod restart counts
kubectl get pods -n redwood | grep prefill | awk '{print $1,$4}'
```
Draining will move new prefills off the noisy node to healthier pool members.

anne_oncall: Bob — confirm when prefetch flag flipped. David — keep customer updated that we're redirecting traffic to fallback and may temporarily trim very long prompts if needed.

bob_infra: Prefetch=false pushed. Observability shows a drop in sustained GPU memory allocations for new prefill sessions. Restart rate fell from 18->4 in last 5m.

eve_customer_eng: Customer asked if there's a safe workaround on their side besides trimming: recommended sending shorter prefill chunks or using streaming chunking to avoid single huge prefill. They appreciate the transparency.

carla_sre: After cordon/drain node-3, restarts on that node stopped. Other nodes still occasionally restart when they receive a very large prefill. I suggest we also enable a temporary token-length cap for prefill on this pool to 65k and log-truncate beyond that so we avoid evictions.

anne_oncall: Implementing token cap via runtime config now (hot reload). Command: POST /runtime/configs/pool/prefill-gpu-pool-3 {"prefill_max_tokens":65000}. Will monitor.

bob_infra: Config applied. New telemetry shows median prefill memory use down 30%. Restart count now 0 in last 10m for pool.

david_support: Customer update: sent note that we routed their heavy requests to fallback and applied protective caps. Will follow up with post-incident summary and recommended client changes.

anne_oncall: Handoff: I'm handing the incident to night SRE rotation @carla_sre for continued monitoring and postmortem write-up. Key follow-ups for postmortem: root-cause analysis of KV cache growth during prefetch, quantify impacted customer requests, and propose long-term fixes (e.g., automatic prefill trimming, backpressure at edge, preemption-friendly allocation).

carla_sre: Acknowledged — will continue monitoring and start a timeline. I'll coordinate with runtime team for a deeper kernel trace capture and with infra to test a fix that avoids forcing large contiguous device allocations.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigations applied (prefetch disabled, node drained, prefill cap applied). Immediate customer impact reduced. Incident severity downgraded to P2.

eve_customer_eng: I'll prepare a customer-facing postmortem blur for cust-57 draft and loop in support.

anne_oncall: Thanks everyone. I'll add notes to the incident log and open a follow-up ticket for model/runtime changes. Postmortem ETA 48h.

carla_sre: Leaving handoff comment: keeping alerting thresholds tighter on prefill memory for 24h. Will escalate if restarts reappear.

bob_infra: One action item: add a runtime safeguard to refuse single-request prefill allocations > 80% of GPU memory. Filed infra-4372.

david_support: Closing customer loop once we have postmortem. For now, customer satisfied with mitigation.

anne_oncall: Closing thread for live mitigation. Postmortem thread will be separate. :v:
